Subject: Northbridge pilot: isolated VPC/on-prem feasibility & one-week surge ask

Team,

Northbridge Health (external contact Alex Dunn) just sent an initial statement-of-work proposing a 6-week pilot with two options: an isolated VPC deployment in AWS (customer-managed VPC peering + strict audit logs) and an on-prem appliance we’d ship and support for restricted facilities. They expect a short, concentrated ingestion surge during week 2 (~3-4x baseline token throughput for 7 days).

Attachments: nb_sow_v1.pdf, nb_network_diagram_v2.png, pilot_staffing_estimate.xlsx (attached).

High-level asks from my side:
- Can the runtime be delivered in an isolated VPC with their networking constraints (no public EIPs to model endpoints, mutual TLS to the control plane)?
- What extra engineering time and runbook/oncall coverage will an on-prem appliance require (including HSM/KMS integration)?
- For the 1-week surge, what is the minimum staffing/ops commitment to guarantee latency SLOs (and what cost uplift should we expect)?

Please reply with: short constraints we need from the customer (bandwidth, disk for model cache, firewall rules), rough FTE-week estimates for both deployment options, and any hard blockers (e.g., unsupported kernel/path on their hardware, regulatory gaps).

I’d like to sync in a short cross-functional call tomorrow if possible — propose 11:00am PT. If people can’t make that, flag availability.

Thanks,
Marissa

Marissa — thanks for the summary and attachments. Quick technical read:

1) VPC option (short):
- Feasible if they accept our isolated endpoint model (private ALB in their VPC + VPC endpoint to control plane).
- Need explicit network requirements: peak ingress RPS, expected average sequence length (tokens per request), and KV-cache disk requirements.
- Ops-wise: packaging is straightforward; runtime is compatible with current kernels. Estimated effort: ~1 infra engineer (full-time) + 0.5 runtime engineer for ~2 weeks to stand up pilot and validate perf.

2) On-prem appliance (longer):
- This is more involved: we need a signed appliance (container + small control-plane shim), packaging for their on-prem hypervisor, and HSM/KMS integration for key management (they specified HSM).
- Possible blockers: their hardware must support our preferred quantization kernel (A100 or similar recommended). If they have older GPUs or CPU-only, we need to qualify model size and fallback path (quantized LLMs vs. trimmed model).
- Estimated effort: 1.5 infra + 1 runtime + 0.5 security for ~6-8 weeks (including build, secure key path validation, and test harness).

3) Surge handling:
- If surge is limited to 7 days at 3-4x, we can absorb with temporary capacity burst on Dedicated or via short-term GPU burst in their VPC (if permitted). If on-prem, we need clear headroom on their hardware — otherwise we must ship additional capacity (costly).
- Ops needs a playbook: pre-surge health check, temporary autoscale thresholds, and a rollback policy.

I attached a quick staffing estimate (pilot_staffing_estimate.xlsx) with week-by-week FTEs and a first-pass cost uplift. Also note: network egress and audit log forwarding (to their SIEM) will require TCP/HTTPS outbound allowances.

Karthik

Thanks for looping us in. Operational notes from an SRE/ops perspective:

- Oncall and runbook: we need a named oncall rota for the pilot period (pilot + 2 weeks). For a 1-week surge we require dedicated coverage during business hours + an escalation path for P1s overnight. That typically means 1 primary + 1 secondary (shared).
- Observability: must confirm that audit logs (authN/authZ, model-inference logs) can be forwarded to their SIEM. If they mandate log retention >90 days in a particular region, we will need storage/workflow changes.
- Backups & cache warming: for latency SLOs during surge, pre-warm model caches and ensure snapshot/restore cadence is locked. That requires a 48–72 hour prep window.
- Capacity coordination: if we rely on cloud burst for VPC, we need a capacity reservation or fast procurement — ops lead time is ~72 hours for GPU acquisition.

Soft blockers: their network diagram shows an on-prem NAT gateway with strict outbound filtering. If outbound TLS to our control plane is blocked (IP ranges), we need a pre-approved IP allowlist.

Action: I can draft a runbook template and a surge checklist if we confirm option and dates.

— Soojin
Senior SRE, Redwood Inference

Quick legal/procurement note:

- We need to add explicit language in the SOW for audit log access, data residency, and key custody. If they insist on HSM-managed keys and no key export, security must validate our remote attestation flow. That will add legal review time.
- Procurement: their PO + standard Data Processing Agreement (DPA) will take ~30–45 days to complete on their side. If they want the pilot sooner, we can run a non-production PO but that requires signoff from finance.
- Insurance/indemnity: the SOW should cap liability during pilot and clarify support SLAs (response vs. resolution times).

Please flag if Northbridge will require SOC2 + evidence or penetration test reports; we’ll surface what we can without blocking the pilot (we can provide SOC2 Type II report, standard security questionnaire answers, and a SOC evidence bundle under NDA).

— Priya
